thread:
Mia Chen: heads up — saw a perf regression on the nvprof run from last night. throughput for batch=8 dropped ~9% on the long-seq workload. perfetto shows kernel choice flipping mid-request and NVTX ranges for per-request spans are missing so the timeline is noisy. link: https://perfetto.local/trace/1769543209
perf-bot: perf-tests/throughput/long-seq — FAILED (regression: -9%). compare: 1769450000 -> 1769543209. attached nsys/nvprof zips in artifacts.
Devon Patel: thanks — can you attach the nsys and perfetto files? also which commit?
Mia Chen: commit 9d3f4b2, artifacts:/artifacts/ci/1769543209/nsys.zip and /artifacts/ci/1769543209/perfetto.pbz. perfetto timeline: lots of small kernels interleaved, but the kernel selector metadata isn't annotated so it's hard to tell why it picked the qc8_fast variant on a few requests.
Ashley Rivera: my gut: KV cache prefetch changed timing so a different kernel path got picked for ~20% of requests. If we don't have request-level NVTX ranges we can't correlate selector decisions to request characteristics.
Samir Gupta: agreed. we should add a lightweight per-request NVTX span and also NVTX events when the kernel selector picks a kernel. but need to be careful about overhead and name explosion in perf tools — long names will fragment flamegraphs.
Leo Horvath: +1 on both. prefer short stable span names for grouping, and put variable data in the NVTX payload (not the visible name). Perfetto groups by the visible string so "req=abcd|kvcache_prefetch" will create tons of unique rows.
Ashley Rivera: proposal for naming: use component:phase for the visible range name (e.g., "kvcache:prefetch", "kern:select", "req:handler") and then encode metadata in the nvtx payload as ASCII: "req=abcd;len=64;bucket=16-128;sel=qc8_fast". That lets perf tools group by name and we can search payloads for details.
Samir Gupta: implementation snippet (C++ nvtx):
```
char buf[128];
int n = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "req=%s;len=%d;sel=%s", short_req_id, seq_len, kernel_name);
nvtxEventAttributes_t attr = {0};
attr.version = NVTX_VERSION;
attr.size = NVTX_EVENT_ATTRIB_STRUCT_SIZE;
attr.colorType = NVTX_COLOR_ARGB;
attr.color = 0xFF2B8CDB;
attr.messageType = NVTX_MESSAGE_TYPE_ASCII;
attr.message.ascii = buf;
nvtxRangePushEx(&attr);
// ... work
nvtxRangePop();
```
Samir Gupta: note: payload is limited so keep it short (short_req_id = first 8 chars sha1). also only emit detailed payloads when trace-level flag enabled; otherwise push a minimal range with no payload.
Devon Patel: how about sampling? only annotate 1% of production requests for detailed payloads and do full annotation in debug/dedicated runs. we can also have a per-capture env var that forces all spans for an nsys capture.
Mia Chen: good. what about span bucketing idea — we wanted to group by sequence-length bins to compare kernel decisions across bins. any naming ideas?
Leo Horvath: keep visible name like "req:handler" and add an integer bucket tag in the payload e.g., "b=3" for 256-512. Perf dashboard can group by span name and then parse payload to aggregate by bucket. I'll add parser support.
Ashley Rivera: also instrument kernel selector with a short event: push range "kern:select" for the selection call, payload "sel=qc8_fast;reason=latency_opt;ver=2" — that makes mapping selection to kernel executions much easier in traces.
Samir Gupta: we should also annotate when KV cache prefetch hits vs miss; add spans "kvcache:prefetch" (payload "h=hit") and "kvcache:prefetch" (payload "h=miss") — same visible name, different payload. that keeps rows small.
Devon Patel: next: anyone want to own the changes? I'll take wiring request id through the API and emitting minimal ranges. Ashley take kvcache path, Samir add selector payloads and example code, Leo update perf dashboard grouping/parsing, Mia coordinate tests and rollout.
Mia Chen: plan: feature-flag gated, start with debug builds + CI perf job runs. measure instrumentation overhead with a small nsys job (no payload vs payload) — target <2% overhead. create a small unit test that asserts nvtx push/pop pairs for each request path. also add an e2e perfetto sample in artifacts for future debugging.
Devon Patel: I'll open PRs today for the request-id propagation and a small helper nvtx util (thin wrapper to avoid accidental heavy allocations).
Ashley Rivera: PR for kvcache changes coming from me — will add both hit/miss spans and the prefetch timing. I'll include a toggle so payloads are only emitted when ENABLE_TRACE_PAYLOADS is on.
Samir Gupta: I'll add the kernel-selector ranges and a short test that verifies the payload content is formatted correctly. also will run an nsys baseline to measure overhead.
Leo Horvath: I'll add Perfetto parsing code and update the perf dashboard to group by visible range and expose payload filters.
Mia Chen: thanks all — once we have the new traces we can rerun the failing CI trace and see whether the kernel flip correlates with kvcache behavior. assigning followups in ticket RUN-4525. :thumbsup:
Devon Patel: :thumbsup:
Ashley Rivera: :rocket:
Samir Gupta: noted, will post nsys numbers in the thread.
perf-bot: CI artifact uploaded: /artifacts/ci/1769543210/instrumentation-proof.png
Mia Chen: perfect — dropping the perfetto link + next steps in RUN-4525.
